title: KV drum-buffering with on-the-fly page compression and swap-rate throttling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Prototype a paged/blocked KV cache variant that combines a small in-GPU resident working set (hot window), a drum-style on-GPU staging buffer for short-lived pages, and compressed cold pages stored within GPU memory to reduce swap churn. Goal: reduce tail latency and OOM incidents during demand spikes while keeping per-token cost down for typical chat generation workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Integration prototype runs on a 8xA100 cluster and handles synthetic spike workload without OOM for 95% of runs
End-to-end p99 latency regression <= +10% compared to baseline under steady load
Net GPU memory usage reduction >= 18% for long-context Llama-like models with LZ4-lite enabled
Documented knobs for drum buffer size, compression window, and swap-rate throttle exposed to runtime config
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff - agreed on two-stage strategy (hot window + drum buffer) and microbench design. Design doc created: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runtime/kv-drum-buffer-v1
2026-03-11: Implemented drum buffer ring with lock-free producer/consumer path in C++ runtime. Basic allocation path integrated with existing slab allocator.
2026-03-12: Added LZ4-lite compress/decompress path for page marshaling; CPU overhead measured and adjusted threshold to only compress pages older than 2s.

2026-03-12: First integration tests with continuous-batching harness. Observed 22% reduction in physical page swaps but +6% CPU usage on scheduler host. Logged benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426

2026-03-13: Implemented swap-rate shear-throttle that enforces a max swaps/sec per-GPU and gracefully delays demotions rather than dropping requests. Tuned default throttle to 40 swaps/sec on 80GB Vram targets.
benchmarks: Microbench (synthetic long-context chat, batch sizes 1-8): baseline p50/p95/p99 = 12/48/130 ms, prototype = 13/52/138 ms
Memory delta (Llama-70B-like): baseline GPU resident = 72GB, prototype with compression = 58.6GB (-18.8%)
Swap churn: baseline average swaps/min during spike = 340, prototype = 115 (-66%), swaps/sec capped at configured throttle = 38
CPU overhead: scheduler host +6% average CPU during compression windows (mitigated via async worker pool)
decisions: Use ephemeral drum buffer on GPU rather than moving cold pages back to host DRAM for typical spikes because host transfer latency causes worse p99s for continuous-batching workloads.
Adopt LZ4-lite (reduced compression ratio but low CPU cost) as default compressor for in-GPU compressed pages. FP16/quantized storage considered but deferred due to model correctness risks.
Swap-rate shear-throttle implemented as a soft limiter with exponential backoff for repeated demotion attempts to avoid cascading OOMs.
Eviction policy: epoch-based demotion first, then age-weighted LRU within drum buffer. Full eviction only when swap-rate throttle exceeded and free memory still low.
tradeoffs: Pros: significant reduction in host<->GPU PCIe transfers and fewer OOMs during spikes; flexible knobs for operators.

Cons: additional complexity in runtime; modest CPU cost for compression; potential mismatches with model-internal KV semantics if page boundaries collide with attention cache expectations (mitigation: atomic reassembly in runtime).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: compression-induced latency spikes on low-CPU hosts - mitigate by detecting host load and disabling compression when CPU headroom < 20%.
Risk: data corruption during aggressive demotion - mitigation: add CRC checks in page header and defensive rehydration path that falls back to host-resident cold page when CRC fails.

Risk: customers doing deterministic replay across versions may see differences if compressed pages introduced - mitigation: compression is configurable per-deployment and off by default for Dedicated/Private until validated.
